text:
sam: heads-up — I sketched a minimal handoff contract between the weight loader and the warmup/prefetch layer. main goals: atomic handoff, eviction fence, and manifestless token so Dedicated can stream shards without races.

ali: show the sketch pls — curious how you avoid double-fetches when we have partial network failures :thinking:

sam: gist: loader returns a lightweight Lease object that represents ownership of a shard range. lease has states (pending, ready, retired). warmup can start reading from pending but must not publish pointers until ready. eviction only allowed if retired. snippet: 

```
struct Lease {
  ShardID id;
  enum State {PENDING, READY, RETIRED};
  uintptr_t gpu_ptr; // 0 if not ready
  Token lease_token; // used for atomic swap in page tables
};

Lease request_lease(ShardID);
void retire_lease(Token);
```

tess: ok but who owns the fallback path? if warmup sees network hiccup and lease never transitions to READY, we need a sync fallback that doesn't race with a late READY. maybe a versioned token?

sam: planned: lease_token is monotonic version + uuid. fallback path does a compare-and-swap on page-table entry: CAS(expected=0 or older_token, new=lease_token). only when CAS succeeds do we treat gpu_ptr as authoritative. if later READY arrives with same token we fast-path.

kevin: CAS on page-table is sensible. question: what about safetensors sharded on object storage with partial-range availability? can we stream subranges while holding a lease?

sam: yes. lease can be subshard-range aware. request_lease takes (shard_id, byte_range). loader will fetch and populate incremental checkpoints and mark READY once bounds used by runtime are present. warmup should prefer prefix hydration.

ali: but we still need an eviction fence for the case where runtime wants to evict but loader is mid-write and READY never arrives. how do we prevent corrupted pointers?

sam: eviction flow: retire_lease(token) sets state RETIRED and increments epoch; retire only allowed by token owner. retire triggers an ordered write to page-table replacing token with tombstone. if loader later tries to publish with older token CAS will fail and it must free partial allocations.

tess: sounds good. can we embed a short TTL for pending leases so we don't leak GPU allocations on long network stalls? also need metrics: pending->ready latency, CAS failures, orphaned-retire counts.

sam: TTL yes, default 30s for hosted mode, configurable per-customer for Dedicated. metrics + alerting planned.

kevin: concern: when we do prefix streaming into KV cache and then a topology change migrates the shard to another server, who transfers lease? do we allow lease handoff across nodes?

sam: we support inter-node lease transfer via a transfer_token. flow: source retires and emits transfer_token; dest claims with claim_transfer(transfer_token) which does atomic swap on central manifest to avoid split-brain. ephemeral manifests stored in the control-plane for transfers.

ali: that adds control-plane dependency — ok for Dedicated but for Private/offline customers?

sam: for on-prem we have optional gossip-based transfer where nodes sign transfer_token and peer verifies signature, same exact CAS on local page-tables. documented fallback path in the RFC doc.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: noted: add feature flag "lease_handoff_v1" gated rollout to 10% first. :eyes:

tess: next steps: write a tiny reference impl in rust/python to validate CAS semantics and simulate races. I'll pair with sam tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — I'll open a short RFC follow-up with the pseudo-API, state machine diagram, and test matrix. will include sample logs and error codes.

kevin: one more: test idea — inject delayed READY after retire to ensure cleanup path and no leaked pointers. add to chaos suite.

sam: added. end.
